title: Limit the task run per EventLoop tick via a timeout

timeline.message:
Limit the task run per EventLoop tick via a timeout

Motivation:

We should better allow to limit the number of tasks that are run per EventLoop tick via a timeout. This timeout can be adjusted by -Dio.netty.eventLoop.maxTaskProcessingDurationPerRun

Modifications:

Change property name and set default to 1 second.

Result:

Fixes https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/14165
timeline.author: Norman Maurer

timeline.body:
Motivation:

We should better allow to limit the number of tasks that are run per EventLoop tick via a timeout. This timeout can be adjusted by -Dio.netty.eventLoop.maxTaskProcessingQuantumMs

Modifications:

Change property name and set default to 1 second.

Result:

Fixes https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/14165

I have another question. 
Should we use the `final` to modify the maxTaskDurationPerRun field? 

Perhaps we could provide a `setMaxTaskDurationPerRun` method to allow users to adjust the configuration of their ioEventLoop?
this is a best effect (soft limit), not a hard limit too, I'm not sure the property name

reply.body: I am open for better naming.

timeline.body:
> I have another question. Should we use the `final` to modify the maxTaskDurationPerRun field?
> 
> Perhaps we could provide a `setMaxTaskDurationPerRun` method to allow users to adjust the configuration of their ioEventLoop?

If we want we can add a constructor parameter for it... But I wanted to keep it simple for now.
Let's use 100 ms which is the default CFS period (see https://docs.kernel.org/scheduler/sched-bwc.html)

reply.body: @franz1981 do you think this is enough ? I just wonder if this might let tasks grow.

@franz1981 Do you want to use 100 ms for the minimum quantum, or for the maximum? When I first saw your comment I thought you meant maximum quantum, so as to improve responsiveness in case we get more I/O work while working on the tasks, but on second reading I realize it's not fully clear which one you mean.
Max :) Sorry i haven't explained properly
In operating system lingo I think this is called a quantum, so it could also be `io.netty.eventLoop.maxTaskProcessingQuantumSoftLimit`, but He-Pin's suggestion is also fine.
Can we include the units in the name of the property to avoid confusion and incorrect units? `io.netty.eventLoop.maxTaskProcessingQuantumNsSoftLimit`

+1 to @Scottmitch's suggestion of including units in the name although the units look like their in ms and typically the units are at the end. I'd personally go with `io.netty.eventLoop.maxTaskProcessingQuantumMs` but don't have strong opinions other than including the units.

timeline.body: There are some good suggestions from others I'd also like to see, but I'll pre-approve here.

timeline.author: Norman Maurer

timeline.body: @franz1981 is this what you had in mind ?

timeline.author: Norman Maurer
Norman Maurer

timeline.body:
Yeah, in CFS this should be the target latency within a process should get its guaranteed fair schedule/chance to run IIRC.
And here, have a similarish meaning i.e. I/O will get its chance to run after this, although with a delay (our tasks are not preemptive).

TBH what CFS does is to update via a timer (the OS tick rate) the virtual time of the task running on CPU, guaranteed a min granularity time to run on the CPU or eventually perform a different decision if there are more.
